title: Automattic has a new board after failed attempt to put CEO on leave
slides: Automattic's board shake-up: what really happened?
Failed attempt to put CEO on leave
But new board members may challenge him
Watch for policy shifts at WordPress and Tumblr
Boards that move early shape company direction
thread_text:
1. The boardroom coup that wasn't

Automattic's board tried to put CEO Matt Mullenweg on leave. It failed — but the fight is far from over.

2. The failed leave attempt

A majority of the board voted to sideline Mullenweg. He refused. The move exposed a deeper power struggle over control.

3. New board members, new threats

Fresh faces on the board aren't loyalists. They're already questioning Mullenweg's decisions on WordPress and Tumblr.

4. Policy shifts are coming

Watch for changes to WordPress dot com's moderation rules, Tumblr's content policies, and how Automattic handles its open-source community.

5. What boards do early matters

If you're building a company, decide now: who has real power when the CEO and board clash? Test your own governance plan with a simple scenario.

instagram.caption:
A majority of Automattic's board voted to put CEO Matt Mullenweg on leave. He refused, and the attempt failed. 🗳️

Now the company has a new board, and the new members aren't loyalists. They're already questioning his calls on WordPress and Tumblr.

For anyone who publishes on WordPress.com or Tumblr, moderation rules and content policies could shift.

If you run a site on either platform, would you want to know who actually holds power before those changes land?
